description: Decide how much process, escalation and review a situation deserves from how many people are being hurt and whether the harm can be undone - and look harder whenever a small problem recurs.
when_to_apply: deciding whether something is an incident at all
deciding how many people to page
deciding how large a post-incident review should be
a small event has happened before
steps: Estimate the blast radius: who is hurt now, and how many.
Ask whether the harm can be undone; treat irreversible harm as large regardless of reach.
Estimate how much time you have before the harm grows.
Choose the smallest process that fits: ticket, short review, or full incident process.
Escalate a small, repeated event: three occurrences are a pattern.
quality_indicators: the effort spent was proportionate to the harm
irreversible harm always got the full process
failure_modes: running the full process for everything, which costs more than the incidents
dismissing each recurrence as small on its own
example: A three-minute authentication blip gets a half-page review instead of a full postmortem - but because it is the third since spring, the half page must answer what changed before each one.
